rootCauses: Mac and Linux omitted --ansi, so the previous helper always suppressed the code even at sufficient width; Windows always supplied width0.
COLUMNS alone could be unset/stale; stdout redirection requires the caller to pass measured TTY/Console dimensions.
Block-font leading breaks finder patterns in actual Menlo raster; the long-URL red is preserved. Final ANSI rendering uses solid background double-space modules.
Mac browser menu immediately covered the code; QR now stays visible and enter opens the existing menu. Exercising paused input exposed zsh read -t .1; corrected to0.1 in both Mac copies.

displayContract.ansi: Whole QR modules use background40/47 and two spaces; required dimensions are2N+2 columns andN+6 rows, with four-module quiet zone. No block glyph dependency.
displayContract.plain: NO_COLOR including empty disables ANSI; visible character code remains but its polarity is not counted as a portable phone-scanning guarantee.
displayContract.insufficientSizeOrColor: Mac automatically opens only own generated local PNG in Preview; Linux uses xdg-open only when a graphical session exists; Windows requests own PNG only in an interactive local desktop. Unavailable preview is explicitly incomplete with PNG/URL/HTML retained.
displayContract.loopback: All loopback entries are labelled only-this-machine, phone unavailable. No instance is exposed.
displayContract.multipleCards: Primary first input is painted last so its QR remains visible after scroll; file order is unchanged.
displayContract.nonTTY: No input wait; Mac no GUI launch; URL/HTML/PNG retained.
